Pratipa.note: King of the Kuru line; husband of Sunanda.

Devapi.note: Eldest son of Pratipa; a skin ailment led him to renounce the throne and take to the forest, which is why the throne passed to his younger brother Shantanu instead. Held by tradition to be alive still, a chiranjivi in the hidden village of Kalapa alongside the Ikshvaku king Maru, and expected to return and revive both the solar and lunar lines when the Kali age ends.

Bahlika.note: Son of Pratipa; ruled the Bahlika kingdom. His descendants fought on the Kaurava side; an elder at the Kuru court through the whole epic, present at the dice game and every council, too bound by kinship to Duryodhana to leave despite disapproving of the war, and killed at Kurukshetra by Bhima on the seventeenth day.

Shantanu.note: Youngest son of Pratipa; became king when Devapi renounced. Father of Bhishma. Married Ganga on the condition he never question her, and lost her when he broke it over the drowning of their eighth son; years later fell for the fisherman's daughter Satyavati, whose father would only give her if her sons inherited the throne — the demand that made Bhishma take his vow of celibacy.

Bhurishravas.note: Son of Somadatta; a mighty Kaurava warrior slain by Satyaki at Kurukshetra.

Bhishma.note: Born Devavrata; took a vow of lifelong celibacy so his father could marry Satyavati, hence 'Bhishma'. He was Prabhasa, the eighth and last of the eight Vasus, cursed to a long mortal life for stealing the sage Vasishtha's cow; his seven brother-Vasus, shown here as Ganga's other sons, she returned at once to heaven. Grandsire and regent of the Kurus; a chiranjivi who chose his own hour of death. By name — abducting Amba, Ambika and Ambalika at their swayamvara for Vichitravirya, releasing Amba when she loved another, her vow of revenge and rebirth as Shikhandi, ten days commanding the Kaurava host at Kurukshetra, falling pierced by Arjuna's arrows through Shikhandi shielding him, lying on that bed of arrows through the rest of the war, and teaching Yudhishthira statecraft from it before choosing to die at the sun's turn north (uttarayana).

VasuDhara.name: Dhara
VasuDhara.note: A Vasu, deva of the earth; a brother-Vasu of Bhishma (Prabhasa), borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuDhruva.name: Dhruva
VasuDhruva.note: A Vasu, deva of the pole star; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuSoma.name: Soma
VasuSoma.note: A Vasu, deva of the moon; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuAha.name: Aha
VasuAha.note: A Vasu, deva of the day and the ethereal space; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuAnila.name: Anila
VasuAnila.note: A Vasu, deva of the wind; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuAnala.name: Anala
VasuAnala.note: A Vasu, deva of fire (Agni); borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

VasuPratyusha.name: Pratyusha
VasuPratyusha.note: A Vasu, deva of the dawn; borne by Ganga and returned to heaven.

Vyasa.note: Born to Satyavati by Parashara on an island in the Yamuna, hence Krishna Dvaipayana. He divided the one Veda into four because the age had grown too dull to hold it whole, fathered Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura by niyoga, and composed the epic his own descendants are the cast of. The seventeenth of the avatars, SB 1.3.21. By name — compiling the eighteen Puranas and the Brahma Sutras, dictating the Mahabharata to Ganesha on condition the god never pause for an unintelligible verse, appearing at need throughout the epic to guide his line (granting Sanjaya far-sight to narrate the war, consoling Dhritarashtra, giving Gandhari the vision of her dead sons one last night), and, in the Bhagavata's own frame, the guru who taught it entire to his son Shukadeva.

Chitrangada.note: Elder son of Shantanu and Satyavati; a proud king slain young by a gandharva, leaving no heir. Killed in single combat by a gandharva of the very same name, who considered himself the only rightful bearer of it; his death, without a son, is what put Vichitravirya and then the niyoga line on the Kuru throne instead.

Vichitravirya.note: Younger son of Shantanu and Satyavati; wed Ambika and Ambalika but died childless, prompting the niyoga that continued the line. Both wives were won for him by Bhishma at their own swayamvara, abducted from the assembled kings of Kashi; Vichitravirya himself took no part in winning them, and died of consumption within a few years of the marriage, worn out, without an heir.

Dhritarashtra.note: Born blind to Ambika through Vyasa's niyoga; the elder prince, kept from the throne by his blindness. Father of the Kauravas. By name — his blind favouritism toward Duryodhana through every wrong, from the lac-house to the dice game to the war itself; crushing an iron statue of Bhima to pieces after the war, meant for the real man, on Krishna's warning; and retiring to the forest with Gandhari and Kunti in his last years, dying with them in a forest fire.

Pandu.note: Born pale to Ambalika through Vyasa's niyoga; king of Hastinapura. Shot the sage Kindama and his wife while they were coupling in the form of deer, not knowing them for sages, and was cursed to die the instant he embraced a wife in desire — so his five sons were begotten on Kunti's and Madri's mantras by the devas instead. Died breaking that vow at last with Madri, who followed him onto the pyre.

Vidura.note: Born to the maid Parishrami through Vyasa's niyoga; an incarnation of Dharma, wisest counsellor of the Kurus, never king by birth of a servant. By name — the Vidura-niti, his counsel to Dhritarashtra against the dice game and the war, ignored every time; warning Yudhishthira of the lac-house plot in riddles the Pandavas alone understood; and retiring at the very end to the forest, where he is said to have poured his own life into Yudhishthira at their last meeting before dying.

Duryodhana.note: Eldest of the hundred Kauravas; the crown prince whose enmity for the Pandavas drove the war. At his birth jackals howled, an omen he should be cast out. By name — the lac-house at Varanavata built to burn the Pandavas alive, the rigged dice game that won Yudhishthira's kingdom and Draupadi, her disrobing in the Kuru hall that Krishna alone answered, refusing even five villages to avoid war, crowning Karna king of Anga against his own house's objections, eighteen days directing the Kaurava host after Bhishma, Drona and Karna each fell, and dying on the war's last day with his thigh broken by Bhima's mace, the blow Bhima had sworn at the dice game.

Dushasana.note: Second Kaurava; dragged Draupadi into the assembly and tried to disrobe her, an outrage Bhima avenged by tearing open his breast.

Dushala.note: The only daughter of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, born after the hundred sons; wed to Jayadratha, king of Sindhu.

Yuyutsu.note: Son of Dhritarashtra by the maid Sughada; the one son of that house to cross over and fight on the Pandava side.

Lakshmanaa.note: Daughter of Duryodhana; carried off by Krishna's son Samba, which nearly sparked a war.

LakshmanaK.name: Lakshmana
LakshmanaK.note: Son of Duryodhana (Lakshmana Kumara); slain by Abhimanyu inside the chakravyuha.

Yudhishthira.note: Eldest Pandava, begotten of Kunti by Dharma (Yama); the just king, never known to lie. By name — winning Draupadi's hand for all five brothers by his mother's unwitting word, founding Indraprastha, the Rajasuya that provoked Duryodhana's envy, losing the kingdom, his brothers, Draupadi and himself at dice, thirteen years' exile including one incognito as Kanka in Virata's court, answering the Yaksha's riddles at the lake to revive his brothers, king again after the war, the Ashvamedha that followed, and at the very end walking to heaven with a dog who was Dharma himself, refusing to abandon it at the gate.

Bhima.note: Second Pandava, begotten of Kunti by Vayu; of superhuman strength, sworn to kill all hundred Kauravas. By name — killing the rakshasa Bakasura to free a village, marrying the rakshasi Hidimba and fathering Ghatotkacha, surviving Duryodhana's poisoning and a river-drowning to gain a naga boon of tenfold strength, killing Kichaka in Virata's court for molesting Draupadi, drinking Dushasana's blood at Kurukshetra as sworn over Draupadi's disrobing, and ending the war breaking Duryodhana's thigh in their mace duel.

Arjuna.note: Third Pandava, begotten of Kunti by Indra; the supreme archer, friend of Krishna, hearer of the Bhagavad Gita. By name — winning Draupadi at her svayamvara by the fish-eye shot, the pilgrimage-exile and marriages to Chitrangada and Ulupi, burning Khandava forest beside Krishna and meeting Agni and Mayasura there, winning Subhadra, the year as Brihannala in Virata's court, penance on Himavat for the Pashupata from Shiva and weapons from the other lokapalas, charioteer scene and the Gita at Kurukshetra, killing Bhishma from behind Shikhandi, Jayadratha within a day as sworn, Karna at last, the post-war Ashvamedha campaign, and the Mahaprasthana into the Himalayas at the end with his brothers.

Nakula.note: Fourth Pandava, twin son of Madri by the Ashvins; matchless horseman and the handsomest of men.

Sahadeva.note: Youngest Pandava, twin son of Madri by the Ashvins; wisest of the brothers and a knower of the future.

Prativindhya.note: Son of Yudhishthira and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.

Sutasoma.note: Son of Bhima and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.

Shrutakarma.note: Son of Arjuna and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.

Shatanika.note: Son of Nakula and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.

Shrutasena.note: Son of Sahadeva and Draupadi; one of the Upapandavas.

Ghatotkacha.note: Son of Bhima and Hidimba; a rakshasa prince of great sorcery who grew to manhood in a day and died turning the tide of the war, drawing Karna's infallible weapon onto himself.

Barbarika.note: Son of Ghatotkacha; the archer of the three arrows who vowed to fight for whichever side was losing and so gave up his head to Krishna. Came to Kurukshetra with a bow that needed only three arrows to end any war — one to mark every target, one to mark himself, one to finish it; Krishna, seeing he would keep his vow to the losing side over and over and so make the war endless, begged his head as alms before the fighting began; set on a hill, the head watched the whole eighteen days and, asked afterward who really won, said only that it saw Krishna's chakra everywhere the fighting was.

Abhimanyu.note: Son of Arjuna and Subhadra; the boy warrior who broke into the chakravyuha and was killed within it, leaving Uttara pregnant with the Kuru line's sole heir.

Parikshit.note: Son of Abhimanyu and Uttara; stillborn but revived by Krishna, he became the sole surviving heir and king of the Kurus after the war.

Janamejaya.note: Son of Parikshit; the king at whose serpent sacrifice the Mahabharata was first recited, by Vaishampayana, Vyasa's own disciple. Began the sacrifice to avenge his father's death by Takshaka's bite, and kept it burning until Astika, kin to both the sacrificer's court and the nagas being fed into the fire, won a boon before Janamejaya knew what he was granting and made him stop with Vasuki, Takshaka and the rest of the naga race still unburned.

ShatanikaII.name: Shatanika
ShatanikaII.note: Son of Janamejaya (not to be confused with the Upapandava of the same name); he carried the Kuru throne into the age after the war.

Ashwamedhadatta.note: Son of Shatanika; a later Kuru king. The Puranas run the line on through several more kings to Kshemaka, its last.

Samvarana.note: King of the Kuru line who wed Tapati, Surya's daughter; father of Kuru, the dynasty's eponym.

people.Viduratha: Son of Kuru; carries the throne onward through Jahnu's branch.

ParikshitI.name: Parikshit
ParikshitI.note: Kuru-line king; not the Parikshit of the Mahabharata's own generation, born generations earlier. Namesake, see PURANIC_LINEAGES.md Part V.

people.Bhimasena: Kuru-line king, father of Pratishravas. Not the Pandava Bhima.
people.Anjanaparvan: Son of Ghatotkacha and Maurvi; a rakshasa prince of the Bhima line.

Parikshi.note: Eldest son of Kuru, who left no sons. SB 9.22.4, 9.22.9

Sudhanu.note: Son of Kuru, from whom the line runs to Uparichara Vasu and thence to Magadha, Matsya and Chedi. SB 9.22.4-6

JahnuK.name: Jahnu
JahnuK.note: Son of Kuru. The Bhagavata runs the Kuru succession through him; this tree keeps the Mahabharata's line through Viduratha, and both are recorded. SB 9.22.4, 9.22.9

NishadhaK.name: Nishadha
NishadhaK.note: Youngest son of Kuru. Not Nishadha of the solar line, nor Nala's kingdom. SB 9.22.4

ChyavanaK.name: Chyavana
ChyavanaK.note: Not Chyavana the Bhargava sage, nor Chyavana of Panchala. SB 9.22.5

UparicharaVasu.name: Uparichara Vasu
UparicharaVasu.note: King of Chedi, called Uparichara, the sky-goer, for the crystal chariot Indra gave him. His sons became the kings of Chedi, of Magadha and of Matsya, and his daughter, born of a fish, became Satyavati. SB 9.22.6; MBh 1.57

unions.note: These eight are the Vasus of SB 6.6.10 in a later birth: cursed by Vasishtha for carrying off his cow, they asked Ganga to bear and drown them so the curse would be short, and she did, seven times. Shantanu stopped her hand at the eighth, and so Prabhasa, whose theft it had been, had to live the whole of it out as Bhishma. MBh 1.93-94
